links.outcome: Patient preference, clarity, terminology accessibility and understandability of operative reports
links.effect: 55.4% (95% CI: 48.6%-61.2%) preferred GPT-simplified reports; clearer (mean = 1.53 ± 0.83 vs. 1.98 ± 1.92, P < 0.001); terminology more accessible (mean = 1.50 ± 0.70 vs. 2.31 ± 0.89, P < 0.001); more understandable (mean = 86.40 ± 18.07 vs. 73.70 ± 20.82, P < 0.001); bachelor's degree and below preferred GPT version in 59.6% (95% CI: 52.0%-67.0%)
links.tradeoff: Preferences varied by patient demographics, indicating a need for individualized approaches; only about 55% preferred the simplified version.
links.quote: The primary outcome showed that 55.4% (95% CI: 48.6%-61.2%) of participants preferred the GPT-simplified reports for being significantly clearer (mean = 1.53 ± 0.83 vs. 1.98 ± 1.92, P < 0.001), terminology being more accessible (mean = 1.50 ± 0.70 vs. 2.31 ± 0.89, P < 0.001), and overall, more understandable (mean = 86.40 ± 18.07 vs. 73.70 ± 20.82, P < 0.001).

design_hint: reading-level simplification of patient documents with physician review
